behavior.recording: Gateway takes viewer identity from the authenticated account userId, ignores a legacy body viewerId, canonicalizes UUIDs, and allows viewing a foreign target.
behavior.analyticsReads: Both GET routes verify the current account/profile ownership through Profile RPC with a three-second bound, strict canonical account/profile echoes and owned === true; owned secondary profiles work, foreign or missing profiles are denied before Social.
behavior.errors: Missing or malformed account principal returns 401; invalid target or limit returns 400; foreign/missing ownership returns 403; malformed or unavailable ownership proof maps to 503 before Social.
behavior.privacy: Social writes an acknowledgement and projects timestamp-only recent views; direct Social RPC exposes the same reduced projection. The bounded newest-100 source summary uses direct/profile/search/feed/other; unknown legacy source labels map to other.
behavior.limitsAndLegacyData: Recent-view limits default to 10 and cap at 100; uppercase legacy target UUIDs are queried case-insensitively. Historical viewer IDs are not rewritten or treated as verified ownership; export disposition remains J23/J24.
behavior.staleSelection: The private E2E moves the selected profile owner after token issuance, confirms both analytics reads deny the still-valid signed selection, and restores the profile row.
behavior.client: Existing client wrapper types match timestamp-only responses; no UI component or generated SDK change was introduced.

proof: Real Auth, Profile and Social TCP services behind a production Gateway controller/AuthGuard mini HTTP server.
Body viewerId spoof is ignored; authenticated account UUID is stored when recording a view of a foreign target.
Bearer and cookie sessions can read their actually owned profiles, including a secondary profile with legacy uppercase account ownership.
Foreign/missing target reads are denied; malformed input, invalid limits, stale signed profile ownership, counterpart projections and fixture cleanup are checked.
Direct Social RPC and Gateway endpoints return timestamp-only recent-view objects; counterpart Profile rows and seeded analytics rows remain unchanged.

limitations: Internal service communication remains a trusted TCP boundary.
Ownership RPC waits are configured at three seconds. Malformed replies and mocked RPC failure mapping have unit evidence; no timer-expiry assertion or live Profile outage was run.

The private harness hosts the production controller and AuthGuard with real Auth/Profile/Social services; it is not a full Gateway deployment, browser journey, external-provider run, remote CI run or production qualification.
Bounded result counts and readbacks do not prove database query cancellation or a byte-level retention guarantee.
